title: In this school, no kid has ever owed lunch money

lines.text: In this school, no kid has ever owed lunch money. *Not once*.
Rich kids, poor kids, it doesn't matter. Everyone's balance is always *zero*.
Except *me*. I've never paid for a single lunch.
My mom works two jobs. Some weeks, the fridge is *empty*.
But every day, Miss Rosa gives me the *biggest* tray.
And she always says the same thing. Eat, mijo. It's *paid*.
Miss Rosa walks to work. Even in the *rain*.
And every Friday, she stays late, counting her *own* money at the register.
On her last day before retiring, I found her notebook.
Twenty years of names. Hundreds of kids. Every lunch she paid for, with her *own* salary.
On the very last page, was *my* name.
The kids. The teachers. Even the kids she fed twenty years ago, who were grown up now.
That afternoon, the whole town lined up outside the cafeteria.
Miss Rosa cried. Then she smiled, and said, Eat, mijo. It's *paid*.
In this school, no kid ever owes lunch money. Because someone always *pays*.
